title: Tensor pool siphon and KV-cache journal healing for cross-env GPU OOMs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported recurring GPU OOMs over several weeks. Investigation shows memory fragmentation inside the tensor arena combined with an accumulation of KV-cache tombstones and a small journal corruption case that prevented safe compaction. Symptoms: sudden long-tail OOMs during bursty chat workloads, elevated swap/spill rates on affected nodes, and per-tenant session degradation (requests timing out or tail-latency spikes).

Root cause hypothesis: three interacting issues: (1) the tensor arena grew with many short-lived allocations that left small free slices (slab scattering) because allocation sizes changed between batched requests, (2) KV-cache metadata produced repeated tombstones for long-lived sessions (prefix caching + incremental edits) and our existing tombstone compactor was blind to a subtle journal race, and (3) the journal replay occasionally left duplicate index entries that prevented reclaiming tombstone slots. Together these prevented the allocator from finding contiguous space for large attention tensors, leading to OOMs that were difficult to reproduce in unit tests.

Proposed fix: Implement a two-part runtime patch: (A) Tensor-pool siphon (background migrator) — a low-priority worker that incrementally identifies long-lived, low-touch tensors and migrates them to a spillable pool optimized for coalesced freeing, plus opportunistic slab coalescing to reduce fragmentation. The siphon exposes graceful backpressure and per-tenant caps so migration cannot starve active requests. (B) KV-cache journal heal — a safe journal-replay and index-reconciliation step that removes duplicate tombstone references and reclaims index slots without stopping the runtime (uses a per-node journal checkpoint token and idempotent repair records). The heal also extends the tombstone compactor to do bounded concurrent compaction during low-load windows.

Mitigations applied to customers: emergency memory backpressure tune deployed (hosted) and manual session-eviction for highest-impact Dedicated clusters. For Private customers we provided a diagnostic script and recommended a short maintenance window to apply the livepatch.

Telemetry & detection added: kvcache_tombstones_total, kvcache_journal_inconsistencies, tensor_arena_fragmentation_ratio, tensor_arena_freeable_bytes, siphon_migrated_bytes, spill_evictions_per_minute. Alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.45 sustained for 10m triggers PagerDuty on-call.

Rollout plan: canary (1%) on hosted (runtime-2.4-canary), observe 24h, increase to 10% then 50% over 72h if no regressions; Dedicated clusters: coordinate with SRE and affected customers for staged upgrades (canary host pools then all); Private: provide hotpatch bundle + instructions and offer on-site upgrade for high-impact customers. Backout plan: toggle runtime feature-flag to disable siphon and journal-heal; fallback path to force full offline compaction and revert to previous runtime if needed.

Testing: unit tests for journal-replay idempotency, e2e stress with mixed-length batched workloads (100k sessions), and chaos test that kills siphon mid-migration. Performance targets: added CPU overhead < 4% at steady state and no request latency increase > 2nd percentile.

Customer communications: draft posted to Confluence and to customers with mitigation steps, RCA timeline, and ETA for full rollout.

Artifacts & links: Confluence postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Tensor+pool+siphon+postmortem ; Diagnostic script: https://drive.google.com/rd/diagnostics/tensor_arena_dump.sh ; GitHub PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1182 ; Telemetry dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-memory/tensor-arena-overview

Next steps: finish PR review, run extended hosted canary, coordinate Dedicated customer upgrade windows, and produce a short postmortem and KTL for SREs to reduce time-to-detect.
acceptance_criteria: Canary % rollout shows no regression in 48h across percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
kvcache_journal_inconsistencies drops to zero post-heal on impacted nodes
tensor_arena_fragmentation_ratio reduces by >=30% on affected hosts within 24h
No new customer escalations for GPU OOMs in affected clusters for 7 days
Runtime CPU overhead < 4% at steady state in bench harness
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha K: Initial triage — elevated OOMs correlated with long-lived chat sessions and a dual spike in tombstones and fragmentation. Raised P0 and paged SRE. Added temporary backpressure knobs to hosted clusters (deployed).

2026-03-04 - Liam O: Root-cause reproduction harness: created mixed-batch stress test that reproduces fragmentation in 6-8 hours on local dev rigs. Found journal replay race when two compactions interleave. PoC siphon implemented and prevented OOM in harness. (PR draft created).
2026-03-06 - QA: Ran regression test suite (nightly) — siphon caused negligible p50 change but increased background CPU by ~3%. Added a low-priority scheduling limit to siphon.
2026-03-08 - SRE: Hosted canary 1% started at 02:00 UTC. No OOM regressions to date. Added dashboard panels for new metrics.

2026-03-09 - Customer ops: Dedicated customer ARC-57 requested immediate patch; scheduled hotpatch window and applied binary with siphon disabled + manual journal heal. ARC-57 confirmed reduced tail-latency after reclaim.

2026-03-11 - Engineering review: Security reviewed journal-replay logic for TAMpering/consistency — no permission escalation. Decided to gate heal behind node-level checkpoint token to protect concurrent writers.
2026-03-12 - Liam O: PR merged to canary track (runtime-2.4-canary). Preparing canary increase to 10% pending 24h clean run. Drafting customer-facing RCA for affected tenants.
